# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1466
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1466
- **Title**: gh-1455 [BUG] bash_job stop cancelled the whole run + teardown crash (StreamSink double-bind) hung fa until bench stall-kill — probe r5 get-bitcoin-nodes
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1455` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +486
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T23:37:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T00:21:44Z

## PR Description

Closes #1455
### Root Cause

Three shutdown-isolation defects, one incident: (1) `shellTool` forwarded the
run's `CancelToken` into every `jobs.start()` `ShellExecOptions`, so any run
teardown (`Agent.abort`, idle watchdog, signal) killed every live background
job — and a `bash_job stop` racing that unwind aborted the phase mid-batch;
(2) the headless HEP/stream-json writers fired an unawaited `stdout.flush()`
per frame, and `stdout` throws a synchronous `StateError("StreamSink is bound
to a stream")` when a write/flush overlaps an in-flight flush — an uncaught
zone error (crash.log) that also wedged the exit path until the runner
stall-kill; (3) `agent_loop._errorToolResult` rendered a tool-level
`CancelledException` with the "uncaught exception inside the harness tool
implementation" hint, telling the model its bash tool was broken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart`: registry firewall — caller cancel tokens
  never reach job space; jobs are stopped only via `ShellJobEntry.stop`.
- `lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart`: no run token into job starts; a
  genuine run-shutdown cancel during a foreground-as-job bash hands the
  still-running job to the background (the same handback as a steering
  yield) instead of killing it. The stuck-call supervisor's `cancel_retry`
  cancel (`StuckCallFollowUp` on the call token) deliberately keeps its
  cancel-and-retry semantics — the call fails like before, the job lives.
- `bin/fah_util.dart`: one serialized, guarded write+flush chain for all HEP
  and stream-json lines (`_enqueueStdoutLine`/`drainStdoutLines`); the exit
  paths (`_gracefulHeadlessExit`, the `finally` flushes in
  `bin/fah_runapp.dart`) drain the chain instead of racing it.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`: on an aborted turn, headless fa exits
  promptly — prints the honest detach summary and skips the job-drain
  rounds and the `--wait-for-jobs` ceiling.
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`: `CancelledException` renders as
  `Tool error (bash): run was aborted — tool not started (cancel reason: …)`
  — no harness-defect hint; the cancel reason (e.g. the watchdog summary)
  stays on the record.

### Test Coverage

- `test/tools/shell_jobs_run_token_isolation_test.dart` — 2 tests, both
  failed before the fix (job killed by the caller token; `Bad state:
  Command aborted`), pass after.
- `test/agent/tool_cancelled_error_test.dart` — reproduced the exact
  transcript symptom (`Tool error (bash): CancelledException: …` + hint),
  passes after.
- `test/integration/headless_hep_teardown_burst_test.dart` — new
  hermetic subprocess test: a 31-turn tool loop through `--output events`
  exits 0 with an intact, ordered frame stream and no `StateError`.
- Full slice runs on the final tree (ambient `FA_*` stripped — the
  integration mocks need that on runners with a live provider queue):
  `test/tools/` + `test/agent/` 970 passed / 0 failed; `test/cli/`
  3409 passed / 0 failed (run in two alphabetical halves — the runner's
  native teardown abort below makes the single-shot run flaky);
  integration pair 5 passed / 0 failed.

### Notes

- Direct `env.startShellJob(cancelToken: …)` callers keep their existing
  contract (the env-level token still kills that job) — the firewall is at
  the tool-facing registry layer.
- The combined-suite runs on this dev runner sometimes abort at
  `dart test` shutdown with `malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`
  (exit 134) AFTER all tests pass. Reproduced identically on the untouched
  baseline commit (`bc46a99`) in a clean worktree — a pre-existing,
  load-dependent VM teardown issue, unrelated to this fix.
- Integration-test hermeticity: Dart's `Process.run(environment:)` MERGES
  with the parent env, so this runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDER_QUEUE` (a live
  failover queue) leaked into mock-LLM subprocess tests and could answer
  off-script. The new burst test uses `includeParentEnvironment: false`;
  the pre-existing `headless_log_file_test.dart` still merges (worth a
  follow-up) — run integration slices with the `FA_*` vars unset.
- Pre-existing wart observed, not fixed here (separate ticket candidate):
  the KB tag generator logs a `[KBTagGeneratorAgent] …` prompt line onto
  stdout, polluting the `--output events` JSONL channel for supervisors.

# gh-1455: [BUG] bash_job stop cancelled the whole run + teardown crash (StreamSink double-bind) hung fa until bench stall-kill — probe r5 get-bitcoin-nodes

## Description

## Bug — bench r5 probe: `bash_job stop` aborted the WHOLE run, then fa crashed in teardown (`Bad state: StreamSink is bound to a stream`) and hung until the bench stall-killed it

Probe run 37922037577 (2 shards, 15 tasks = the 14 round-4 stall victims + hello-world), task **get-bitcoin-nodes** (shard-1), session `2026-10-09T13-06-55_01a120c6-…`, container `b2e04adc733d`.

### Timeline (session + tmux pane)
- 13:06:55 → 13:18:44 — agent healthy and productive (background job `sh-1`/`sh-17` registered, tests self-run PASS, tool results every ~20s; the model's text right before: *"All tests pass — but I spotted an environment gotcha: ps/kill failed… Let me find the PID via /proc, do a real restart, and re-verify."*).
- **13:19:03** — one assistant message carries (thinking, text, toolCall). The model issues a foreground `bash python3 - <<EOF…` **plus stops its background job**: the panel renders `┌─ bash task stopped` / `sh-17 … stopped by user`. The foreground tool returns INSTANTLY: `Tool error (bash): CancelledException — This is an uncaught exception inside the harness tool implementation` (0s — cancelled at start, never ran).
- Same second: final assistant message `stop=aborted`, empty content; panel prints `aborted: Operation aborted` + the `fa-tokens:` summary — the normal Ctrl+C/SIGINT wrap-up path, **but nobody pressed anything**: the bench deadline was 1090s away (fa-agent-timeout.json: single extension `stall_detected at 1090.8s`).
- **Then fa crashed**: `fa crashed: Bad state: StreamSink is bound to a stream` + `details appended to /root/.fah/crash.log` + `Run with --help for usage.` — an unhandled Dart `StateError` (StreamSink double-bind) escaping the shutdown path.
- The pane then sat silent at a shell prompt; the bench progress-watch saw a 360.2s byte gap and stall-killed the leftover at 1090.8s → the task's official outcome is **`stall`** (fa-agent-timeout.json `outcome: "stall"`, `gap_sec: 360.215`, last_progress 730.6s — i.e. the kill landed 6 min AFTER fa's last real output; `bench_metrics` guard `loud_empty ok:false`).

### Two defects
1. **Run-wide cancellation from a job stop**: something in the `bash_job stop` path (registry → `job.stop()` → `_LocalShellJob.stop`) fired the RUN's CancelToken, not just the job's own token ([REDACTED:Sensitive Value] takes a per-job `CancelToken?` — the run-token must not be reachable). Symptom: the NEXT foreground tool starts already-cancelled (`CancelledException` at 0s), the turn aborts with `stop=aborted` as if the user hit Ctrl+C.
2. **Teardown crash + hang**: after the abort wrap-up, an unhandled `Bad state: StreamSink is bound to a stream` crashes the process (crash.log on the runner — container recycled, not exported), and whatever survived kept the agent phase alive for the bench until its stall watchdog reaped it (task misclassified `stall` instead of `completed`/`crashed`; the model had already finished its verification pass).

### Why it matters
- It cost the probe its only non-ceiling anomaly and will misclassify full-bench tasks the same way (verdict pollution: `stall` instead of a real outcome).
- Round-4 sibling family: `tmux-advanced-workflow` died to a model-run `tmux kill-server` — jobs/tools reaching outside their own lifetime is the same class.
- The `CancelledException` result text claims "uncaught exception inside the harness tool implementation… the tool may be unavailable in this environment" — for a deliberate cancellation this message misleads the model (it will avoid the tool).

### Ask
1. RCA + fix: `bash_job stop` cancels ONLY the job (its own token/process group); the run token is unreachable from tool space. Test: run + bg job, stop the job, next foreground tool runs normally; run stays alive.
2. RCA + fix: no `StateError` may escape shutdown (`StreamSink is bound to a stream` — find the double-bound sink in the abort/export path); after an abort, headless fa EXITS promptly (bench-visible: pane closes, agent phase ends without a watchdog).
3. `CancelledException` on a tool start renders as a deliberate cancellation ("run was aborted — tool not started"), not as a harness-internal exception (also feeds the #1444 honest-errors family).

### Evidence paths (exported)
`/tmp/probe/extracted_merged/shard-1/get-bitcoin-nodes/…`: `panes/post-agent.txt` (the crash print), `agent-logs/fah-sessions/--app--/2026-10-09T13-06-55-*.jsonl` (103 recs, tail = the cancelled pair), `agent-logs/fa-agent-timeout.json` + `hang-1090.json` (stall misclassification), `agent-logs/bench_metrics.json` (`loud_empty` ok:false).

### References
#1122 (progress-watch policy — its json documented this), #1392 (progress-watch creation), #517/#925/#562 (shell-job family: groups, log sink, settle), gh-1053 (tree kills), #1444 (honest error text family). Round-4 context: #1406.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

{"content":"# Rework — gh-1455 shutdown isolation (PR #1466)

## Issues/Notes

- **Previous head was red; this rework head is a fresh head.** The prior head
  `653839ab5` went red in validation (1/3 per the owner directive). The branch
  has since merged current `main` (`7e0c3a137`), so validation now runs against
  a **new head** — the "3 reds on the same head" latch does not apply.
- `input/gh-1455/ci_failures.md` reports **no failed checks** on this rework
  head; `ci_failures_full.log` does not exist. No merge-conflict markers,
  no open review threads (`pr_discussions_raw.json` → `"threads": []`).
- No code changes were required in this leg — the fix was re-verified as-is
  on the new head (see Test Coverage). One observation carried from the PR
  description (not fixed here, separate ticket candidate): the KB tag
  generator logs a `[KBTagGeneratorAgent] …` prompt line onto stdout,
  polluting the `--output events` JSONL channel.

## Approach

Re-verified the three-defect fix on the merged head instead of re-writing it:

1. **Run-wide cancellation from a job stop** — caller cancel tokens no longer
   reach job space: `ShellJobRegistry.start` drops `options.cancelToken`
   (registry firewall), `shellTool` no longer forwards the run token into job
   starts, and a run-token cancel during foreground-as-job bash unwinds via
   the background handback (same path as a steering yield) instead of killing
   the job. The stuck-call supervisor's `StuckCallFollowUp` cancel keeps its
   cancel-and-retry semantics: the call fails (`Command aborted`), the job
   lives.
2. **Teardown crash + hang** — all HEP/stream-json stdout writes now go
   through one serialized, guarded write+flush chain
   (`_enqueueStdoutLine`/`drainStdoutLines` in `bin/fah_util.dart`); every
   exit path (`_gracefulHeadlessExit`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart` finally flushes)
   drains the chain instead of racing a bare `stdout.flush()` — the exact
   `StateError("StreamSink is bound to a stream")` source. On an aborted
   turn, headless fa prints the honest detach summary and skips the
   job-drain rounds / `--wait-for-jobs` ceiling, so it exits promptly.
3. **Misleading CancelledException text** — `agent_loop._errorToolResult`
   renders a tool-level `CancelledException` as
   `Tool error (bash): run was aborted — tool not started (cancel reason: …)`,
   without the harness-defect hint.

## Files Modified

None in this leg (rework was verification-only). The PR's existing changes:

- `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart` — registry firewall: caller cancel tokens
  never reach job space.
- `lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart` — no run token into job starts;
  run-cancel handback; supervisor cancel-retry preserved.
- `bin/fah_util.dart` — serialized guarded stdout write+flush chain;
  `drainStdoutLines()` for exit paths.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — exit-path flushes drain the chain.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` — aborted turns exit promptly with the
  honest detach summary.
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` — `CancelledException` renders as a
  deliberate cancellation, not a harness defect.
- Tests: `test/tools/shell_jobs_run_token_isolation_test.dart`,
  `test/agent/tool_cancelled_error_test.dart`,
  `test/integration/headless_hep_teardown_burst_test.dart`.

## Test Coverage

All runs on head `7e0c3a137` (ambient `FA_*` vars stripped for the
integration mocks, per the PR's hermeticity note):

- Focused PR tests: `test/tools/shell_jobs_run_token_isolation_test.dart` +
  `test/agent/tool_cancelled_error_test.dart` — **3 passed / 0 failed**.
- `test/integration/headless_hep_teardown_burst_test.dart` — **1 passed /
  0 failed** (31-turn HEP burst, exit 0, ordered intact frame stream).
- `dart analyze bin/fah_util.dart bin/fah_runapp.dart` — no issues.
- `test/tools/` + `test/agent/` — **996 passed / 0 failed**.
- `test/cli/` — full slice result appended below.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1466
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1466
- **Title**: gh-1455 [BUG] bash_job stop cancelled the whole run + teardown crash (StreamSink double-bind) hung fa until bench stall-kill — probe r5 get-bitcoin-nodes
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1455` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +486
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T23:37:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T00:21:44Z

## PR Description

Closes #1455
### Root Cause

Three shutdown-isolation defects, one incident: (1) `shellTool` forwarded the
run's `CancelToken` into every `jobs.start()` `ShellExecOptions`, so any run
teardown (`Agent.abort`, idle watchdog, signal) killed every live background
job — and a `bash_job stop` racing that unwind aborted the phase mid-batch;
(2) the headless HEP/stream-json writers fired an unawaited `stdout.flush()`
per frame, and `stdout` throws a synchronous `StateError("StreamSink is bound
to a stream")` when a write/flush overlaps an in-flight flush — an uncaught
zone error (crash.log) that also wedged the exit path until the runner
stall-kill; (3) `agent_loop._errorToolResult` rendered a tool-level
`CancelledException` with the "uncaught exception inside the harness tool
implementation" hint, telling the model its bash tool was broken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart`: registry firewall — caller cancel tokens
  never reach job space; jobs are stopped only via `ShellJobEntry.stop`.
- `lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart`: no run token into job starts; a
  genuine run-shutdown cancel during a foreground-as-job bash hands the
  still-running job to the background (the same handback as a steering
  yield) instead of killing it. The stuck-call supervisor's `cancel_retry`
  cancel (`StuckCallFollowUp` on the call token) deliberately keeps its
  cancel-and-retry semantics — the call fails like before, the job lives.
- `bin/fah_util.dart`: one serialized, guarded write+flush chain for all HEP
  and stream-json lines (`_enqueueStdoutLine`/`drainStdoutLines`); the exit
  paths (`_gracefulHeadlessExit`, the `finally` flushes in
  `bin/fah_runapp.dart`) drain the chain instead of racing it.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`: on an aborted turn, headless fa exits
  promptly — prints the honest detach summary and skips the job-drain
  rounds and the `--wait-for-jobs` ceiling.
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`: `CancelledException` renders as
  `Tool error (bash): run was aborted — tool not started (cancel reason: …)`
  — no harness-defect hint; the cancel reason (e.g. the watchdog summary)
  stays on the record.

### Test Coverage

- `test/tools/shell_jobs_run_token_isolation_test.dart` — 2 tests, both
  failed before the fix (job killed by the caller token; `Bad state:
  Command aborted`), pass after.
- `test/agent/tool_cancelled_error_test.dart` — reproduced the exact
  transcript symptom (`Tool error (bash): CancelledException: …` + hint),
  passes after.
- `test/integration/headless_hep_teardown_burst_test.dart` — new
  hermetic subprocess test: a 31-turn tool loop through `--output events`
  exits 0 with an intact, ordered frame stream and no `StateError`.
- Full slice runs on the final tree (ambient `FA_*` stripped — the
  integration mocks need that on runners with a live provider queue):
  `test/tools/` + `test/agent/` 970 passed / 0 failed; `test/cli/`
  3409 passed / 0 failed (run in two alphabetical halves — the runner's
  native teardown abort below makes the single-shot run flaky);
  integration pair 5 passed / 0 failed.

### Notes

- Direct `env.startShellJob(cancelToken: …)` callers keep their existing
  contract (the env-level token still kills that job) — the firewall is at
  the tool-facing registry layer.
- The combined-suite runs on this dev runner sometimes abort at
  `dart test` shutdown with `malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`
  (exit 134) AFTER all tests pass. Reproduced identically on the untouched
  baseline commit (`bc46a99`) in a clean worktree — a pre-existing,
  load-dependent VM teardown issue, unrelated to this fix.
- Integration-test hermeticity: Dart's `Process.run(environment:)` MERGES
  with the parent env, so this runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDER_QUEUE` (a live
  failover queue) leaked into mock-LLM subprocess tests and could answer
  off-script. The new burst test uses `includeParentEnvironment: false`;
  the pre-existing `headless_log_file_test.dart` still merges (worth a
  follow-up) — run integration slices with the `FA_*` vars unset.
- Pre-existing wart observed, not fixed here (separate ticket candidate):
  the KB tag generator logs a `[KBTagGeneratorAgent] …` prompt line onto
  stdout, polluting the `--output events` JSONL channel for supervisors.

# gh-1455: [BUG] bash_job stop cancelled the whole run + teardown crash (StreamSink double-bind) hung fa until bench stall-kill — probe r5 get-bitcoin-nodes

## Description

## Bug — bench r5 probe: `bash_job stop` aborted the WHOLE run, then fa crashed in teardown (`Bad state: StreamSink is bound to a stream`) and hung until the bench stall-killed it

Probe run 37922037577 (2 shards, 15 tasks = the 14 round-4 stall victims + hello-world), task **get-bitcoin-nodes** (shard-1), session `2026-10-09T13-06-55_01a120c6-…`, container `b2e04adc733d`.

### Timeline (session + tmux pane)
- 13:06:55 → 13:18:44 — agent healthy and productive (background job `sh-1`/`sh-17` registered, tests self-run PASS, tool results every ~20s; the model's text right before: *"All tests pass — but I spotted an environment gotcha: ps/kill failed… Let me find the PID via /proc, do a real restart, and re-verify."*).
- **13:19:03** — one assistant message carries (thinking, text, toolCall). The model issues a foreground `bash python3 - <<EOF…` **plus stops its background job**: the panel renders `┌─ bash task stopped` / `sh-17 … stopped by user`. The foreground tool returns INSTANTLY: `Tool error (bash): CancelledException — This is an uncaught exception inside the harness tool implementation` (0s — cancelled at start, never ran).
- Same second: final assistant message `stop=aborted`, empty content; panel prints `aborted: Operation aborted` + the `fa-tokens:` summary — the normal Ctrl+C/SIGINT wrap-up path, **but nobody pressed anything**: the bench deadline was 1090s away (fa-agent-timeout.json: single extension `stall_detected at 1090.8s`).
- **Then fa crashed**: `fa crashed: Bad state: StreamSink is bound to a stream` + `details appended to /root/.fah/crash.log` + `Run with --help for usage.` — an unhandled Dart `StateError` (StreamSink double-bind) escaping the shutdown path.
- The pane then sat silent at a shell prompt; the bench progress-watch saw a 360.2s byte gap and stall-killed the leftover at 1090.8s → the task's official outcome is **`stall`** (fa-agent-timeout.json `outcome: "stall"`, `gap_sec: 360.215`, last_progress 730.6s — i.e. the kill landed 6 min AFTER fa's last real output; `bench_metrics` guard `loud_empty ok:false`).

### Two defects
1. **Run-wide cancellation from a job stop**: something in the `bash_job stop` path (registry → `job.stop()` → `_LocalShellJob.stop`) fired the RUN's CancelToken, not just the job's own token ([REDACTED:Sensitive Value] takes a per-job `CancelToken?` — the run-token must not be reachable). Symptom: the NEXT foreground tool starts already-cancelled (`CancelledException` at 0s), the turn aborts with `stop=aborted` as if the user hit Ctrl+C.
2. **Teardown crash + hang**: after the abort wrap-up, an unhandled `Bad state: StreamSink is bound to a stream` crashes the process (crash.log on the runner — container recycled, not exported), and whatever survived kept the agent phase alive for the bench until its stall watchdog reaped it (task misclassified `stall` instead of `completed`/`crashed`; the model had already finished its verification pass).

### Why it matters
- It cost the probe its only non-ceiling anomaly and will misclassify full-bench tasks the same way (verdict pollution: `stall` instead of a real outcome).
- Round-4 sibling family: `tmux-advanced-workflow` died to a model-run `tmux kill-server` — jobs/tools reaching outside their own lifetime is the same class.
- The `CancelledException` result text claims "uncaught exception inside the harness tool implementation… the tool may be unavailable in this environment" — for a deliberate cancellation this message misleads the model (it will avoid the tool).

### Ask
1. RCA + fix: `bash_job stop` cancels ONLY the job (its own token/process group); the run token is unreachable from tool space. Test: run + bg job, stop the job, next foreground tool runs normally; run stays alive.
2. RCA + fix: no `StateError` may escape shutdown (`StreamSink is bound to a stream` — find the double-bound sink in the abort/export path); after an abort, headless fa EXITS promptly (bench-visible: pane closes, agent phase ends without a watchdog).
3. `CancelledException` on a tool start renders as a deliberate cancellation ("run was aborted — tool not started"), not as a harness-internal exception (also feeds the #1444 honest-errors family).

### Evidence paths (exported)
`/tmp/probe/extracted_merged/shard-1/get-bitcoin-nodes/…`: `panes/post-agent.txt` (the crash print), `agent-logs/fah-sessions/--app--/2026-10-09T13-06-55-*.jsonl` (103 recs, tail = the cancelled pair), `agent-logs/fa-agent-timeout.json` + `hang-1090.json` (stall misclassification), `agent-logs/bench_metrics.json` (`loud_empty` ok:false).

### References
#1122 (progress-watch policy — its json documented this), #1392 (progress-watch creation), #517/#925/#562 (shell-job family: groups, log sink, settle), gh-1053 (tree kills), #1444 (honest error text family). Round-4 context: #1406.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

{"content":"# Rework — gh-1455 shutdown isolation (PR #1466)

## Issues/Notes

- **Previous head was red; this rework head is a fresh head.** The prior head
  `653839ab5` went red in validation (1/3 per the owner directive). The branch
  has since merged current `main` (`7e0c3a137`), so validation now runs against
  a **new head** — the "3 reds on the same head" latch does not apply.
- `input/gh-1455/ci_failures.md` reports **no failed checks** on this rework
  head; `ci_failures_full.log` does not exist. No merge-conflict markers,
  no open review threads (`pr_discussions_raw.json` → `"threads": []`).
- No code changes were required in this leg — the fix was re-verified as-is
  on the new head (see Test Coverage). One observation carried from the PR
  description (not fixed here, separate ticket candidate): the KB tag
  generator logs a `[KBTagGeneratorAgent] …` prompt line onto stdout,
  polluting the `--output events` JSONL channel.

## Approach

Re-verified the three-defect fix on the merged head instead of re-writing it:

1. **Run-wide cancellation from a job stop** — caller cancel tokens no longer
   reach job space: `ShellJobRegistry.start` drops `options.cancelToken`
   (registry firewall), `shellTool` no longer forwards the run token into job
   starts, and a run-token cancel during foreground-as-job bash unwinds via
   the background handback (same path as a steering yield) instead of killing
   the job. The stuck-call supervisor's `StuckCallFollowUp` cancel keeps its
   cancel-and-retry semantics: the call fails (`Command aborted`), the job
   lives.
2. **Teardown crash + hang** — all HEP/stream-json stdout writes now go
   through one serialized, guarded write+flush chain
   (`_enqueueStdoutLine`/`drainStdoutLines` in `bin/fah_util.dart`); every
   exit path (`_gracefulHeadlessExit`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart` finally flushes)
   drains the chain instead of racing a bare `stdout.flush()` — the exact
   `StateError("StreamSink is bound to a stream")` source. On an aborted
   turn, headless fa prints the honest detach summary and skips the
   job-drain rounds / `--wait-for-jobs` ceiling, so it exits promptly.
3. **Misleading CancelledException text** — `agent_loop._errorToolResult`
   renders a tool-level `CancelledException` as
   `Tool error (bash): run was aborted — tool not started (cancel reason: …)`,
   without the harness-defect hint.

## Files Modified

None in this leg (rework was verification-only). The PR's existing changes:

- `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart` — registry firewall: caller cancel tokens
  never reach job space.
- `lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart` — no run token into job starts;
  run-cancel handback; supervisor cancel-retry preserved.
- `bin/fah_util.dart` — serialized guarded stdout write+flush chain;
  `drainStdoutLines()` for exit paths.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — exit-path flushes drain the chain.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` — aborted turns exit promptly with the
  honest detach summary.
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` — `CancelledException` renders as a
  deliberate cancellation, not a harness defect.
- Tests: `test/tools/shell_jobs_run_token_isolation_test.dart`,
  `test/agent/tool_cancelled_error_test.dart`,
  `test/integration/headless_hep_teardown_burst_test.dart`.

## Test Coverage

All runs on head `7e0c3a137` (ambient `FA_*` vars stripped for the
integration mocks, per the PR's hermeticity note):

- Focused PR tests: `test/tools/shell_jobs_run_token_isolation_test.dart` +
  `test/agent/tool_cancelled_error_test.dart` — **3 passed / 0 failed**.
- `test/integration/headless_hep_teardown_burst_test.dart` — **1 passed /

- `dart analyze bin/fah_util.dart bin/fah_runapp.dart` — no issues.
- `test/tools/` + `test/agent/` — **996 passed / 0 failed**.
- `test/cli/` — full slice result appended below.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1466
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1466
- **Title**: gh-1455 [BUG] bash_job stop cancelled the whole run + teardown crash (StreamSink double-bind) hung fa until bench stall-kill — probe r5 get-bitcoin-nodes
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1455` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +486
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T23:37:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T00:21:44Z

## PR Description

Closes #1455
### Root Cause

Three shutdown-isolation defects, one incident: (1) `shellTool` forwarded the
run's `CancelToken` into every `jobs.start()` `ShellExecOptions`, so any run
teardown (`Agent.abort`, idle watchdog, signal) killed every live background
job — and a `bash_job stop` racing that unwind aborted the phase mid-batch;
(2) the headless HEP/stream-json writers fired an unawaited `stdout.flush()`
per frame, and `stdout` throws a synchronous `StateError("StreamSink is bound
to a stream")` when a write/flush overlaps an in-flight flush — an uncaught
zone error (crash.log) that also wedged the exit path until the runner
stall-kill; (3) `agent_loop._errorToolResult` rendered a tool-level
`CancelledException` with the "uncaught exception inside the harness tool
implementation" hint, telling the model its bash tool was broken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart`: registry firewall — caller cancel tokens
  never reach job space; jobs are stopped only via `ShellJobEntry.stop`.
- `lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart`: no run token into job starts; a
  genuine run-shutdown cancel during a foreground-as-job bash hands the
  still-running job to the background (the same handback as a steering
  yield) instead of killing it. The stuck-call supervisor's `cancel_retry`
  cancel (`StuckCallFollowUp` on the call token) deliberately keeps its
  cancel-and-retry semantics — the call fails like before, the job lives.
- `bin/fah_util.dart`: one serialized, guarded write+flush chain for all HEP
  and stream-json lines (`_enqueueStdoutLine`/`drainStdoutLines`); the exit
  paths (`_gracefulHeadlessExit`, the `finally` flushes in
  `bin/fah_runapp.dart`) drain the chain instead of racing it.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`: on an aborted turn, headless fa exits
  promptly — prints the honest detach summary and skips the job-drain
  rounds and the `--wait-for-jobs` ceiling.
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`: `CancelledException` renders as
  `Tool error (bash): run was aborted — tool not started (cancel reason: …)`
  — no harness-defect hint; the cancel reason (e.g. the watchdog summary)
  stays on the record.

### Test Coverage

- `test/tools/shell_jobs_run_token_isolation_test.dart` — 2 tests, both
  failed before the fix (job killed by the caller token; `Bad state:
  Command aborted`), pass after.
- `test/agent/tool_cancelled_error_test.dart` — reproduced the exact
  transcript symptom (`Tool error (bash): CancelledException: …` + hint),
  passes after.
- `test/integration/headless_hep_teardown_burst_test.dart` — new
  hermetic subprocess test: a 31-turn tool loop through `--output events`
  exits 0 with an intact, ordered frame stream and no `StateError`.
- Full slice runs on the final tree (ambient `FA_*` stripped — the
  integration mocks need that on runners with a live provider queue):
  `test/tools/` + `test/agent/` 970 passed / 0 failed; `test/cli/`
  3409 passed / 0 failed (run in two alphabetical halves — the runner's
  native teardown abort below makes the single-shot run flaky);
  integration pair 5 passed / 0 failed.

### Notes

- Direct `env.startShellJob(cancelToken: …)` callers keep their existing
  contract (the env-level token still kills that job) — the firewall is at
  the tool-facing registry layer.
- The combined-suite runs on this dev runner sometimes abort at
  `dart test` shutdown with `malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`
  (exit 134) AFTER all tests pass. Reproduced identically on the untouched
  baseline commit (`bc46a99`) in a clean worktree — a pre-existing,
  load-dependent VM teardown issue, unrelated to this fix.
- Integration-test hermeticity: Dart's `Process.run(environment:)` MERGES
  with the parent env, so this runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDER_QUEUE` (a live
  failover queue) leaked into mock-LLM subprocess tests and could answer
  off-script. The new burst test uses `includeParentEnvironment: false`;
  the pre-existing `headless_log_file_test.dart` still merges (worth a
  follow-up) — run integration slices with the `FA_*` vars unset.
- Pre-existing wart observed, not fixed here (separate ticket candidate):
  the KB tag generator logs a `[KBTagGeneratorAgent] …` prompt line onto
  stdout, polluting the `--output events` JSONL channel for supervisors.

# gh-1455: [BUG] bash_job stop cancelled the whole run + teardown crash (StreamSink double-bind) hung fa until bench stall-kill — probe r5 get-bitcoin-nodes

## Description

## Bug — bench r5 probe: `bash_job stop` aborted the WHOLE run, then fa crashed in teardown (`Bad state: StreamSink is bound to a stream`) and hung until the bench stall-killed it

Probe run 37922037577 (2 shards, 15 tasks = the 14 round-4 stall victims + hello-world), task **get-bitcoin-nodes** (shard-1), session `2026-10-09T13-06-55_01a120c6-…`, container `b2e04adc733d`.

### Timeline (session + tmux pane)
- 13:06:55 → 13:18:44 — agent healthy and productive (background job `sh-1`/`sh-17` registered, tests self-run PASS, tool results every ~20s; the model's text right before: *"All tests pass — but I spotted an environment gotcha: ps/kill failed… Let me find the PID via /proc, do a real restart, and re-verify."*).
- **13:19:03** — one assistant message carries (thinking, text, toolCall). The model issues a foreground `bash python3 - <<EOF…` **plus stops its background job**: the panel renders `┌─ bash task stopped` / `sh-17 … stopped by user`. The foreground tool returns INSTANTLY: `Tool error (bash): CancelledException — This is an uncaught exception inside the harness tool implementation` (0s — cancelled at start, never ran).
- Same second: final assistant message `stop=aborted`, empty content; panel prints `aborted: Operation aborted` + the `fa-tokens:` summary — the normal Ctrl+C/SIGINT wrap-up path, **but nobody pressed anything**: the bench deadline was 1090s away (fa-agent-timeout.json: single extension `stall_detected at 1090.8s`).
- **Then fa crashed**: `fa crashed: Bad state: StreamSink is bound to a stream` + `details appended to /root/.fah/crash.log` + `Run with --help for usage.` — an unhandled Dart `StateError` (StreamSink double-bind) escaping the shutdown path.
- The pane then sat silent at a shell prompt; the bench progress-watch saw a 360.2s byte gap and stall-killed the leftover at 1090.8s → the task's official outcome is **`stall`** (fa-agent-timeout.json `outcome: "stall"`, `gap_sec: 360.215`, last_progress 730.6s — i.e. the kill landed 6 min AFTER fa's last real output; `bench_metrics` guard `loud_empty ok:false`).

### Two defects
1. **Run-wide cancellation from a job stop**: something in the `bash_job stop` path (registry → `job.stop()` → `_LocalShellJob.stop`) fired the RUN's CancelToken, not just the job's own token ([REDACTED:Sensitive Value] takes a per-job `CancelToken?` — the run-token must not be reachable). Symptom: the NEXT foreground tool starts already-cancelled (`CancelledException` at 0s), the turn aborts with `stop=aborted` as if the user hit Ctrl+C.
2. **Teardown crash + hang**: after the abort wrap-up, an unhandled `Bad state: StreamSink is bound to a stream` crashes the process (crash.log on the runner — container recycled, not exported), and whatever survived kept the agent phase alive for the bench until its stall watchdog reaped it (task misclassified `stall` instead of `completed`/`crashed`; the model had already finished its verification pass).

### Why it matters
- It cost the probe its only non-ceiling anomaly and will misclassify full-bench tasks the same way (verdict pollution: `stall` instead of a real outcome).
- Round-4 sibling family: `tmux-advanced-workflow` died to a model-run `tmux kill-server` — jobs/tools reaching outside their own lifetime is the same class.
- The `CancelledException` result text claims "uncaught exception inside the harness tool implementation… the tool may be unavailable in this environment" — for a deliberate cancellation this message misleads the model (it will avoid the tool).

### Ask
1. RCA + fix: `bash_job stop` cancels ONLY the job (its own token/process group); the run token is unreachable from tool space. Test: run + bg job, stop the job, next foreground tool runs normally; run stays alive.
2. RCA + fix: no `StateError` may escape shutdown (`StreamSink is bound to a stream` — find the double-bound sink in the abort/export path); after an abort, headless fa EXITS promptly (bench-visible: pane closes, agent phase ends without a watchdog).
3. `CancelledException` on a tool start renders as a deliberate cancellation ("run was aborted — tool not started"), not as a harness-internal exception (also feeds the #1444 honest-errors family).

### Evidence paths (exported)
`/tmp/probe/extracted_merged/shard-1/get-bitcoin-nodes/…`: `panes/post-agent.txt` (the crash print), `agent-logs/fah-sessions/--app--/2026-10-09T13-06-55-*.jsonl` (103 recs, tail = the cancelled pair), `agent-logs/fa-agent-timeout.json` + `hang-1090.json` (stall misclassification), `agent-logs/bench_metrics.json` (`loud_empty` ok:false).

### References
#1122 (progress-watch policy — its json documented this), #1392 (progress-watch creation), #517/#925/#562 (shell-job family: groups, log sink, settle), gh-1053 (tree kills), #1444 (honest error text family). Round-4 context: #1406.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

{"content":"# Rework — gh-1455 shutdown isolation (PR #1466)

## Issues/Notes

- **Previous head was red; this rework head is a fresh head.** The prior head
  `653839ab5` went red in validation (1/3 per the owner directive). The branch
  has since merged current `main` (`7e0c3a137`), so validation now runs against
  a **new head** — the "3 reds on the same head" latch does not apply.
- `input/gh-1455/ci_failures.md` reports **no failed checks** on this rework
  head; `ci_failures_full.log` does not exist. No merge-conflict markers,
  no open review threads (`pr_discussions_raw.json` → `"threads": []`).
- No code changes were required in this leg — the fix was re-verified as-is
  on the new head (see Test Coverage). One observation carried from the PR
  description (not fixed here, separate ticket candidate): the KB tag
  generator logs a `[KBTagGeneratorAgent] …` prompt line onto stdout,
  polluting the `--output events` JSONL channel.

## Approach

Re-verified the three-defect fix on the merged head instead of re-writing it:

1. **Run-wide cancellation from a job stop** — caller cancel tokens no longer
   reach job space: `ShellJobRegistry.start` drops `options.cancelToken`
   (registry firewall), `shellTool` no longer forwards the run token into job
   starts, and a run-token cancel during foreground-as-job bash unwinds via
   the background handback (same path as a steering yield) instead of killing
   the job. The stuck-call supervisor's `StuckCallFollowUp` cancel keeps its
   cancel-and-retry semantics: the call fails (`Command aborted`), the job
   lives.
2. **Teardown crash + hang** — all HEP/stream-json stdout writes now go
   through one serialized, guarded write+flush chain
   (`_enqueueStdoutLine`/`drainStdoutLines` in `bin/fah_util.dart`); every
   exit path (`_gracefulHeadlessExit`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart` finally flushes)
   drains the chain instead of racing a bare `stdout.flush()` — the exact
   `StateError("StreamSink is bound to a stream")` source. On an aborted
   turn, headless fa prints the honest detach summary and skips the
   job-drain rounds / `--wait-for-jobs` ceiling, so it exits promptly.
3. **Misleading CancelledException text** — `agent_loop._errorToolResult`
   renders a tool-level `CancelledException` as
   `Tool error (bash): run was aborted — tool not started (cancel reason: …)`,
   without the harness-defect hint.

## Files Modified

None in this leg (rework was verification-only). The PR's existing changes:

- `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart` — registry firewall: caller cancel tokens
  never reach job space.
- `lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart` — no run token into job starts;
  run-cancel handback; supervisor cancel-retry preserved.
- `bin/fah_util.dart` — serialized guarded stdout write+flush chain;
  `drainStdoutLines()` for exit paths.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — exit-path flushes drain the chain.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` — aborted turns exit promptly with the
  honest detach summary.
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` — `CancelledException` renders as a
  deliberate cancellation, not a harness defect.
- Tests: `test/tools/shell_jobs_run_token_isolation_test.dart`,
  `test/agent/tool_cancelled_error_test.dart`,
  `test/integration/headless_hep_teardown_burst_test.dart`.

## Test Coverage

All runs on head `7e0c3a137` (ambient `FA_*` vars stripped for the
integration mocks, per the PR's hermeticity note):

- Focused PR tests: `test/tools/shell_jobs_run_token_isolation_test.dart` +
  `test/agent/tool_cancelled_error_test.dart` — **3 passed / 0 failed**.
- `test/integration/headless_hep_teardown_burst_test.dart` — **1 passed /
  0 failed** (31-turn HEP burst, exit 0, ordered intact frame stream).
- `dart analyze bin/fah_util.dart bin/fah_runapp.dart` — no issues.
- `test/tools/` + `test/agent/` — **996 passed / 0 failed**.
- `test/cli/` — full slice result appended below.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1466
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1466
- **Title**: gh-1455 [BUG] bash_job stop cancelled the whole run + teardown crash (StreamSink double-bind) hung fa until bench stall-kill — probe r5 get-bitcoin-nodes
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1455` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +486
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T23:37:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T00:21:44Z

## PR Description

Closes #1455
### Root Cause

Three shutdown-isolation defects, one incident: (1) `shellTool` forwarded the
run's `CancelToken` into every `jobs.start()` `ShellExecOptions`, so any run
teardown (`Agent.abort`, idle watchdog, signal) killed every live background
job — and a `bash_job stop` racing that unwind aborted the phase mid-batch;
(2) the headless HEP/stream-json writers fired an unawaited `stdout.flush()`
per frame, and `stdout` throws a synchronous `StateError("StreamSink is bound
to a stream")` when a write/flush overlaps an in-flight flush — an uncaught
zone error (crash.log) that also wedged the exit path until the runner
stall-kill; (3) `agent_loop._errorToolResult` rendered a tool-level
`CancelledException` with the "uncaught exception inside the harness tool
implementation" hint, telling the model its bash tool was broken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart`: registry firewall — caller cancel tokens
  never reach job space; jobs are stopped only via `ShellJobEntry.stop`.
- `lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart`: no run token into job starts; a
  genuine run-shutdown cancel during a foreground-as-job bash hands the
  still-running job to the background (the same handback as a steering
  yield) instead of killing it. The stuck-call supervisor's `cancel_retry`
  cancel (`StuckCallFollowUp` on the call token) deliberately keeps its
  cancel-and-retry semantics — the call fails like before, the job lives.
- `bin/fah_util.dart`: one serialized, guarded write+flush chain for all HEP
  and stream-json lines (`_enqueueStdoutLine`/`drainStdoutLines`); the exit
  paths (`_gracefulHeadlessExit`, the `finally` flushes in
  `bin/fah_runapp.dart`) drain the chain instead of racing it.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`: on an aborted turn, headless fa exits
  promptly — prints the honest detach summary and skips the job-drain
  rounds and the `--wait-for-jobs` ceiling.
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`: `CancelledException` renders as
  `Tool error (bash): run was aborted — tool not started (cancel reason: …)`
  — no harness-defect hint; the cancel reason (e.g. the watchdog summary)
  stays on the record.

### Test Coverage

- `test/tools/shell_jobs_run_token_isolation_test.dart` — 2 tests, both
  failed before the fix (job killed by the caller token; `Bad state:
  Command aborted`), pass after.
- `test/agent/tool_cancelled_error_test.dart` — reproduced the exact
  transcript symptom (`Tool error (bash): CancelledException: …` + hint),
  passes after.
- `test/integration/headless_hep_teardown_burst_test.dart` — new
  hermetic subprocess test: a 31-turn tool loop through `--output events`
  exits 0 with an intact, ordered frame stream and no `StateError`.
- Full slice runs on the final tree (ambient `FA_*` stripped — the
  integration mocks need that on runners with a live provider queue):
  `test/tools/` + `test/agent/` 970 passed / 0 failed; `test/cli/`
  3409 passed / 0 failed (run in two alphabetical halves — the runner's
  native teardown abort below makes the single-shot run flaky);
  integration pair 5 passed / 0 failed.

### Notes

- Direct `env.startShellJob(cancelToken: …)` callers keep their existing
  contract (the env-level token still kills that job) — the firewall is at
  the tool-facing registry layer.
- The combined-suite runs on this dev runner sometimes abort at
  `dart test` shutdown with `malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`
  (exit 134) AFTER all tests pass. Reproduced identically on the untouched
  baseline commit (`bc46a99`) in a clean worktree — a pre-existing,
  load-dependent VM teardown issue, unrelated to this fix.
- Integration-test hermeticity: Dart's `Process.run(environment:)` MERGES
  with the parent env, so this runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDER_QUEUE` (a live
  failover queue) leaked into mock-LLM subprocess tests and could answer
  off-script. The new burst test uses `includeParentEnvironment: false`;
  the pre-existing `headless_log_file_test.dart` still merges (worth a
  follow-up) — run integration slices with the `FA_*` vars unset.
- Pre-existing wart observed, not fixed here (separate ticket candidate):
  the KB tag generator logs a `[KBTagGeneratorAgent] …` prompt line onto
  stdout, polluting the `--output events` JSONL channel for supervisors.

# gh-1455: [BUG] bash_job stop cancelled the whole run + teardown crash (StreamSink double-bind) hung fa until bench stall-kill — probe r5 get-bitcoin-nodes

## Description

## Bug — bench r5 probe: `bash_job stop` aborted the WHOLE run, then fa crashed in teardown (`Bad state: StreamSink is bound to a stream`) and hung until the bench stall-killed it

Probe run 37922037577 (2 shards, 15 tasks = the 14 round-4 stall victims + hello-world), task **get-bitcoin-nodes** (shard-1), session `2026-10-09T13-06-55_01a120c6-…`, container `b2e04adc733d`.

### Timeline (session + tmux pane)
- 13:06:55 → 13:18:44 — agent healthy and productive (background job `sh-1`/`sh-17` registered, tests self-run PASS, tool results every ~20s; the model's text right before: *"All tests pass — but I spotted an environment gotcha: ps/kill failed… Let me find the PID via /proc, do a real restart, and re-verify."*).
- **13:19:03** — one assistant message carries (thinking, text, toolCall). The model issues a foreground `bash python3 - <<EOF…` **plus stops its background job**: the panel renders `┌─ bash task stopped` / `sh-17 … stopped by user`. The foreground tool returns INSTANTLY: `Tool error (bash): CancelledException — This is an uncaught exception inside the harness tool implementation` (0s — cancelled at start, never ran).
- Same second: final assistant message `stop=aborted`, empty content; panel prints `aborted: Operation aborted` + the `fa-tokens:` summary — the normal Ctrl+C/SIGINT wrap-up path, **but nobody pressed anything**: the bench deadline was 1090s away (fa-agent-timeout.json: single extension `stall_detected at 1090.8s`).
- **Then fa crashed**: `fa crashed: Bad state: StreamSink is bound to a stream` + `details appended to /root/.fah/crash.log` + `Run with --help for usage.` — an unhandled Dart `StateError` (StreamSink double-bind) escaping the shutdown path.
- The pane then sat silent at a shell prompt; the bench progress-watch saw a 360.2s byte gap and stall-killed the leftover at 1090.8s → the task's official outcome is **`stall`** (fa-agent-timeout.json `outcome: "stall"`, `gap_sec: 360.215`, last_progress 730.6s — i.e. the kill landed 6 min AFTER fa's last real output; `bench_metrics` guard `loud_empty ok:false`).

### Two defects
1. **Run-wide cancellation from a job stop**: something in the `bash_job stop` path (registry → `job.stop()` → `_LocalShellJob.stop`) fired the RUN's CancelToken, not just the job's own token ([REDACTED:Sensitive Value] takes a per-job `CancelToken?` — the run-token must not be reachable). Symptom: the NEXT foreground tool starts already-cancelled (`CancelledException` at 0s), the turn aborts with `stop=aborted` as if the user hit Ctrl+C.
2. **Teardown crash + hang**: after the abort wrap-up, an unhandled `Bad state: StreamSink is bound to a stream` crashes the process (crash.log on the runner — container recycled, not exported), and whatever survived kept the agent phase alive for the bench until its stall watchdog reaped it (task misclassified `stall` instead of `completed`/`crashed`; the model had already finished its verification pass).

### Why it matters
- It cost the probe its only non-ceiling anomaly and will misclassify full-bench tasks the same way (verdict pollution: `stall` instead of a real outcome).
- Round-4 sibling family: `tmux-advanced-workflow` died to a model-run `tmux kill-server` — jobs/tools reaching outside their own lifetime is the same class.
- The `CancelledException` result text claims "uncaught exception inside the harness tool implementation… the tool may be unavailable in this environment" — for a deliberate cancellation this message misleads the model (it will avoid the tool).

### Ask
1. RCA + fix: `bash_job stop` cancels ONLY the job (its own token/process group); the run token is unreachable from tool space. Test: run + bg job, stop the job, next foreground tool runs normally; run stays alive.
2. RCA + fix: no `StateError` may escape shutdown (`StreamSink is bound to a stream` — find the double-bound sink in the abort/export path); after an abort, headless fa EXITS promptly (bench-visible: pane closes, agent phase ends without a watchdog).
3. `CancelledException` on a tool start renders as a deliberate cancellation ("run was aborted — tool not started"), not as a harness-internal exception (also feeds the #1444 honest-errors family).

### Evidence paths (exported)
`/tmp/probe/extracted_merged/shard-1/get-bitcoin-nodes/…`: `panes/post-agent.txt` (the crash print), `agent-logs/fah-sessions/--app--/2026-10-09T13-06-55-*.jsonl` (103 recs, tail = the cancelled pair), `agent-logs/fa-agent-timeout.json` + `hang-1090.json` (stall misclassification), `agent-logs/bench_metrics.json` (`loud_empty` ok:false).

### References
#1122 (progress-watch policy — its json documented this), #1392 (progress-watch creation), #517/#925/#562 (shell-job family: groups, log sink, settle), gh-1053 (tree kills), #1444 (honest error text family). Round-4 context: #1406.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,

## Issues/Notes

- **Previous head was red; this rework head is a fresh head.** The prior head
  `653839ab5` went red in validation (1/3 per the owner directive). The branch
  has since merged current `main` (`7e0c3a137`), so validation now runs against

  on the new head (see Test Coverage). One observation carried from the PR
  description (not fixed here, separate ticket candidate): the KB tag
  generator logs a `[KBTagGeneratorAgent] …` prompt line onto stdout,
  polluting the `--output events` JSONL channel.

## Approach

Re-verified the three-defect fix on the merged head instead of re-writing it:

1. **Run-wide cancellation from a job stop** — caller cancel tokens no longer
   reach job space: `ShellJobRegistry.start` drops `options.cancelToken`
   (registry firewall), `shellTool` no longer forwards the run token into job
   starts, and a run-token cancel during foreground-as-job bash unwinds via
   the background handback (same path as a steering yield) instead of killing
   the job. The stuck-call supervisor's `StuckCallFollowUp` cancel keeps its
   cancel-and-retry semantics: the call fails (`Command aborted`), the job
   lives.
2. **Teardown crash + hang** — all HEP/stream-json stdout writes now go
   through one serialized, guarded write+flush chain
   (`_enqueueStdoutLine`/`drainStdoutLines` in `bin/fah_util.dart`); every
   exit path (`_gracefulHeadlessExit`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart` finally flushes)
   drains the chain instead of racing a bare `stdout.flush()` — the exact
   `StateError("StreamSink is bound to a stream")` source. On an aborted
   turn, headless fa prints the honest detach summary and skips the
   job-drain rounds / `--wait-for-jobs` ceiling, so it exits promptly.
3. **Misleading CancelledException text** — `agent_loop._errorToolResult`
   renders a tool-level `CancelledException` as
   `Tool error (bash): run was aborted — tool not started (cancel reason: …)`,
   without the harness-defect hint.

## Files Modified

None in this leg (rework was verification-only). The PR's existing changes:

- `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart` — registry firewall: caller cancel tokens
  never reach job space.
- `lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart` — no run token into job starts;

- `bin/fah_util.dart` — serialized guarded stdout write+flush chain;

- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — exit-path flushes drain the chain.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` — aborted turns exit promptly with the
  honest detach summary.
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` — `CancelledException` renders as a

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1466
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1466
- **Title**: gh-1455 [BUG] bash_job stop cancelled the whole run + teardown crash (StreamSink double-bind) hung fa until bench stall-kill — probe r5 get-bitcoin-nodes
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1455` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +486
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T23:37:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T00:21:44Z

## PR Description

Closes #1455
### Root Cause

Three shutdown-isolation defects, one incident: (1) `shellTool` forwarded the
run's `CancelToken` into every `jobs.start()` `ShellExecOptions`, so any run
teardown (`Agent.abort`, idle watchdog, signal) killed every live background
job — and a `bash_job stop` racing that unwind aborted the phase mid-batch;
(2) the headless HEP/stream-json writers fired an unawaited `stdout.flush()`
per frame, and `stdout` throws a synchronous `StateError("StreamSink is bound
to a stream")` when a write/flush overlaps an in-flight flush — an uncaught
zone error (crash.log) that also wedged the exit path until the runner
stall-kill; (3) `agent_loop._errorToolResult` rendered a tool-level
`CancelledException` with the "uncaught exception inside the harness tool
implementation" hint, telling the model its bash tool was broken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart`: registry firewall — caller cancel tokens
  never reach job space; jobs are stopped only via `ShellJobEntry.stop`.
- `lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart`: no run token into job starts; a
  genuine run-shutdown cancel during a foreground-as-job bash hands the
  still-running job to the background (the same handback as a steering
  yield) instead of killing it. The stuck-call supervisor's `cancel_retry`
  cancel (`StuckCallFollowUp` on the call token) deliberately keeps its
  cancel-and-retry semantics — the call fails like before, the job lives.
- `bin/fah_util.dart`: one serialized, guarded write+flush chain for all HEP
  and stream-json lines (`_enqueueStdoutLine`/`drainStdoutLines`); the exit
  paths (`_gracefulHeadlessExit`, the `finally` flushes in
  `bin/fah_runapp.dart`) drain the chain instead of racing it.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`: on an aborted turn, headless fa exits
  promptly — prints the honest detach summary and skips the job-drain
  rounds and the `--wait-for-jobs` ceiling.
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`: `CancelledException` renders as
  `Tool error (bash): run was aborted — tool not started (cancel reason: …)`
  — no harness-defect hint; the cancel reason (e.g. the watchdog summary)
  stays on the record.

### Test Coverage

- `test/tools/shell_jobs_run_token_isolation_test.dart` — 2 tests, both
  failed before the fix (job killed by the caller token; `Bad state:
  Command aborted`), pass after.
- `test/agent/tool_cancelled_error_test.dart` — reproduced the exact
  transcript symptom (`Tool error (bash): CancelledException: …` + hint),
  passes after.
- `test/integration/headless_hep_teardown_burst_test.dart` — new
  hermetic subprocess test: a 31-turn tool loop through `--output events`
  exits 0 with an intact, ordered frame stream and no `StateError`.
- Full slice runs on the final tree (ambient `FA_*` stripped — the
  integration mocks need that on runners with a live provider queue):
  `test/tools/` + `test/agent/` 970 passed / 0 failed; `test/cli/`
  3409 passed / 0 failed (run in two alphabetical halves — the runner's
  native teardown abort below makes the single-shot run flaky);
  integration pair 5 passed / 0 failed.

### Notes

- Direct `env.startShellJob(cancelToken: …)` callers keep their existing
  contract (the env-level token still kills that job) — the firewall is at
  the tool-facing registry layer.
- The combined-suite runs on this dev runner sometimes abort at
  `dart test` shutdown with `malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`
  (exit 134) AFTER all tests pass. Reproduced identically on the untouched
  baseline commit (`bc46a99`) in a clean worktree — a pre-existing,
  load-dependent VM teardown issue, unrelated to this fix.
- Integration-test hermeticity: Dart's `Process.run(environment:)` MERGES
  with the parent env, so this runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDER_QUEUE` (a live
  failover queue) leaked into mock-LLM subprocess tests and could answer
  off-script. The new burst test uses `includeParentEnvironment: false`;
  the pre-existing `headless_log_file_test.dart` still merges (worth a
  follow-up) — run integration slices with the `FA_*` vars unset.
- Pre-existing wart observed, not fixed here (separate ticket candidate):
  the KB tag generator logs a `[KBTagGeneratorAgent] …` prompt line onto
  stdout, polluting the `--output events` JSONL channel for supervisors.

# gh-1455: [BUG] bash_job stop cancelled the whole run + teardown crash (StreamSink double-bind) hung fa until bench stall-kill — probe r5 get-bitcoin-nodes

## Description

## Bug — bench r5 probe: `bash_job stop` aborted the WHOLE run, then fa crashed in teardown (`Bad state: StreamSink is bound to a stream`) and hung until the bench stall-killed it

Probe run 37922037577 (2 shards, 15 tasks = the 14 round-4 stall victims + hello-world), task **get-bitcoin-nodes** (shard-1), session `2026-10-09T13-06-55_01a120c6-…`, container `b2e04adc733d`.

### Timeline (session + tmux pane)
- 13:06:55 → 13:18:44 — agent healthy and productive (background job `sh-1`/`sh-17` registered, tests self-run PASS, tool results every ~20s; the model's text right before: *"All tests pass — but I spotted an environment gotcha: ps/kill failed… Let me find the PID via /proc, do a real restart, and re-verify."*).
- **13:19:03** — one assistant message carries (thinking, text, toolCall). The model issues a foreground `bash python3 - <<EOF…` **plus stops its background job**: the panel renders `┌─ bash task stopped` / `sh-17 … stopped by user`. The foreground tool returns INSTANTLY: `Tool error (bash): CancelledException — This is an uncaught exception inside the harness tool implementation` (0s — cancelled at start, never ran).
- Same second: final assistant message `stop=aborted`, empty content; panel prints `aborted: Operation aborted` + the `fa-tokens:` summary — the normal Ctrl+C/SIGINT wrap-up path, **but nobody pressed anything**: the bench deadline was 1090s away (fa-agent-timeout.json: single extension `stall_detected at 1090.8s`).
- **Then fa crashed**: `fa crashed: Bad state: StreamSink is bound to a stream` + `details appended to /root/.fah/crash.log` + `Run with --help for usage.` — an unhandled Dart `StateError` (StreamSink double-bind) escaping the shutdown path.
- The pane then sat silent at a shell prompt; the bench progress-watch saw a 360.2s byte gap and stall-killed the leftover at 1090.8s → the task's official outcome is **`stall`** (fa-agent-timeout.json `outcome: "stall"`, `gap_sec: 360.215`, last_progress 730.6s — i.e. the kill landed 6 min AFTER fa's last real output; `bench_metrics` guard `loud_empty ok:false`).

### Two defects
1. **Run-wide cancellation from a job stop**: something in the `bash_job stop` path (registry → `job.stop()` → `_LocalShellJob.stop`) fired the RUN's CancelToken, not just the job's own token ([REDACTED:Sensitive Value] takes a per-job `CancelToken?` — the run-token must not be reachable). Symptom: the NEXT foreground tool starts already-cancelled (`CancelledException` at 0s), the turn aborts with `stop=aborted` as if the user hit Ctrl+C.
2. **Teardown crash + hang**: after the abort wrap-up, an unhandled `Bad state: StreamSink is bound to a stream` crashes the process (crash.log on the runner — container recycled, not exported), and whatever survived kept the agent phase alive for the bench until its stall watchdog reaped it (task misclassified `stall` instead of `completed`/`crashed`; the model had already finished its verification pass).

### Why it matters
- It cost the probe its only non-ceiling anomaly and will misclassify full-bench tasks the same way (verdict pollution: `stall` instead of a real outcome).
- Round-4 sibling family: `tmux-advanced-workflow` died to a model-run `tmux kill-server` — jobs/tools reaching outside their own lifetime is the same class.
- The `CancelledException` result text claims "uncaught exception inside the harness tool implementation… the tool may be unavailable in this environment" — for a deliberate cancellation this message misleads the model (it will avoid the tool).

### Ask
1. RCA + fix: `bash_job stop` cancels ONLY the job (its own token/process group); the run token is unreachable from tool space. Test: run + bg job, stop the job, next foreground tool runs normally; run stays alive.
2. RCA + fix: no `StateError` may escape shutdown (`StreamSink is bound to a stream` — find the double-bound sink in the abort/export path); after an abort, headless fa EXITS promptly (bench-visible: pane closes, agent phase ends without a watchdog).
3. `CancelledException` on a tool start renders as a deliberate cancellation ("run was aborted — tool not started"), not as a harness-internal exception (also feeds the #1444 honest-errors family).

### Evidence paths (exported)
`/tmp/probe/extracted_merged/shard-1/get-bitcoin-nodes/…`: `panes/post-agent.txt` (the crash print), `agent-logs/fah-sessions/--app--/2026-10-09T13-06-55-*.jsonl` (103 recs, tail = the cancelled pair), `agent-logs/fa-agent-timeout.json` + `hang-1090.json` (stall misclassification), `agent-logs/bench_metrics.json` (`loud_empty` ok:false).

### References
#1122 (progress-watch policy — its json documented this), #1392 (progress-watch creation), #517/#925/#562 (shell-job family: groups, log sink, settle), gh-1053 (tree kills), #1444 (honest error text family). Round-4 context: #1406.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:
